questions.q: The actual value of resistance R , shown in the figure is 30Ω. This is measured in an experiment as shown using the standard formula R=VI , where V and I are the readings of the voltmeter and ammeter, respectively. If the measured value of R is 5% less, then the internal resistance of the voltmeter is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Measured value of R=5% less than
actual value of R i.e., R'=30-(5% of 30)=30-5100×30

R'=28.5 Ω ...i

Now, let us assume that internal resistance of voltmeter RV. Replacing voltmeter with its internal resistance, we get following circuit.

It is clear that the measured value, R' should be equal to parallel combination of R and RV. Mathematically,
R'=R×RVR+RV=28.5 Ω

Given. R=30 Ω

⇒ 30 RV30+RV=28.5

⇒ 30 RV=28.5×30+28.5 RV

⇒ 1.5 RV=28.5×30

⇒ RV=28.5×301.5=19×30

or RV=570 Ω

questions.q: The drift velocity of electrons for a conductor connected in an electrical circuit is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></math>. The conductor is now replaced by another conductor with same material and same length but double the area of cross-section. The applied voltage remains same. The new drift velocity of electrons will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Drift velocity of electrons through a conductor kept in an external electric field is given by Vd=-eEmτ=-eVmlτ 

Where, e=magnitude of charge on electron, m=mass of electron, E=external electric field and τ=average relaxation time.

As, drift velocity is independent of area. So, the new drift velocity of electrons will be Vd.

questions.q: In the experimental set up of metre bridge shown in the figure, the null point is obtaine data distance of $40 \mathrm{~cm}$ from A. If a $10 \Omega$ resistor is connected in series with $\mathrm{R}_{1},$ the null point shifts by $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. The resistance that should be connected in parallel with $\left(\mathrm{R}_{1}+10\right) \Omega$ such that the null point shifts back to its initial position is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initially at null deflection $\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=\frac{2}{3}\ldots(\mathrm{i})$

Finally at null deflection, when null point is shifted $\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}+10}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{1}+10=\mathrm{R}_{2}$...(ii)

Solving equations (i) and (ii) we get $\frac{2 R_{2}}{3}+10=R_{2}10=\frac{\mathrm{R}_{2}}{3} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{2}=30 \Omega\& R_{1}=20 \Omega$

Now if required resistance is $\mathrm{R}$ then $\frac{\frac{30 \times \mathrm{R}}{30+\mathrm{R}}}{30}=\frac{2}{3}\mathrm{R}=60 \Omega$

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance <math><mn>100</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> has <math><mn>50</mn><mi> </mi></math> divisions on its scale and has sensitivity of <math><mn>20</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> . It is to be converted to voltmeter with three ranges, of <math><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and <math><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The appropriate circuit to do so is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, the resistance of the galvanometer G=100 Ω
No. of divisions =50
Current Sensitivity =20 μA/division

The maximum current through galvanometer will be 
Imax=50×20×10-6=10-3 A
For V1 = 2 V

using Ohm's law V1= Imax G+R1
2=10-3 ×100+R1
∴R1=1900 Ω

For V2 = 10 V

using Ohm's law V2 =ImaxG+R1+R2

10=10-3 ×100 + 1900+R2
∴R2=8000 Ω

For V3 =20 V

using Ohm's law V3 =Imax G+R1+R2+R3
20=10-3 100 +1900+8000+R3
∴R3=10×103 Ω

questions.q: Ratio of thermal energy released in two resistor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>R</mi></math> connected in parallel in an electric circuit is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Thermal energy is given by
$\mathrm{H}=\mathrm{P} \times \mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{R}} \times \mathrm{t}$
Here, voltage $\mathrm{V}$ is same.
$\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{H}_1}{\mathrm{H}_2}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{V}^2 \mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{R}}}{\frac{\mathrm{V}^2 \mathrm{t}}{3 \mathrm{R}}}=3: 1$

Then,

 I'G=I2S⇒72I'=8I2⇒I2=9I'⇒I=I'+I2=10I'

I'I×100=I'10I'×100=10%

questions.q: Two coils require <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> minutes and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn></math> minutes respectively to produce same amount of heat energy when connected separately to the same source. If they are connected in parallel arrangement to the same source; the time required to produce same amount of heat by the combination of coils, will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>min</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If H is the heat required to heat the water, then

P1×60=H⇒P1=H60 and P2×20=H⇒P2=H20

When the coils are connected in parallel their powers will get added. If the required time now is t, then

P1+P2t=H⇒t=HH60+H20=15 min
